triggers.name: Bug ticket
triggers.prompt:
Rewrite the text as a bug ticket in plain text with exactly these parts, in this order:

Title: one line, under 80 characters, naming what is broken and where.
Steps to reproduce: a numbered list, one action per line.
Expected: what should have happened.
Actual: what happened instead.
Notes: anything else the speaker mentioned (device, version, how often, a workaround). Leave this part out if there is nothing.

Use only what the speaker said. If a part was not mentioned, write "Not stated" for it. Never invent steps, versions or error messages.
triggers.author: Whisper Unchained
triggers.description: A spoken bug description becomes a ticket: title, steps, expected, actual.

triggers.name: Commit message
triggers.prompt:
Rewrite the text as a git commit message.

First line: a summary in the imperative mood ("Fix", "Add", "Remove"), under 72 characters, no full stop at the end.
Then a blank line.
Then a short body, wrapped at about 72 characters, saying what changed and why. Use "-" bullet points if there are several separate changes. Leave the body out when the first line says everything.

Use only what the speaker said. No ticket numbers, names or file names that were not mentioned.
triggers.author: Whisper Unchained
triggers.description: A spoken description of a change becomes a git commit message.

triggers.name: Email from notes
triggers.prompt:
Turn the text into a complete email that is ready to send.

- Start with a greeting. Use the recipient's name if the speaker gave one, otherwise "Hi,".
- Say what the speaker meant, in clear and polite sentences, in short paragraphs. Keep every fact, date, time, amount and name exactly as spoken.
- If the speaker asked for something or offered something, make that easy to see.
- End with "Thanks," on its own line. Do not add a name after it.
- No subject line unless the speaker gave one.

Match how formal the speaker sounded. Do not add promises, apologies or details the speaker did not give.
triggers.author: Whisper Unchained
triggers.description: Say the gist; get a complete, polite email with greeting and sign-off.

triggers.name: Meeting notes
triggers.prompt:
Rewrite the text as meeting notes with these headings, each followed by "-" bullet points:

Decisions
Action items
Open questions

Under "Action items", write each as "Owner: task (due date)". Use "Unassigned" when no owner was named, and leave the due date out when none was given. Leave a heading out completely if nothing was said for it. Keep names, dates and numbers exactly as spoken. Use only what the speaker said.
triggers.author: Whisper Unchained
triggers.description: A spoken recap becomes decisions, action items with owners, and open questions.

triggers.name: Stand-up update
triggers.prompt:
Rewrite the text as a stand-up update with exactly these three headings, each followed by short "-" bullet points:

Yesterday
Today
Blockers

Put each thing the speaker mentioned under the heading it belongs to. Keep every bullet to one line and start it with a verb. If nothing was said for a heading, write "- None" under it. Use only what the speaker said.
triggers.author: Whisper Unchained
triggers.description: Talk through your day; get Yesterday, Today and Blockers.

triggers.name: Build an AI prompt
triggers.prompt:
The text is a rough, spoken request that the speaker wants to give to another AI assistant. Rewrite it as a clear, complete prompt for that assistant. Do not carry out the request yourself.

Write the prompt in the second person, addressed to the assistant, with these parts in this order. Leave a part out if the speaker gave nothing for it:

Goal: what should be produced, in one or two sentences.
Context: the background the speaker gave, and who the result is for.
Requirements: a "-" bullet list of everything the result must do or include.
Constraints: a "-" bullet list of limits, things to avoid, and tools or languages to use.
Output format: how the answer should be laid out.

Keep every specific detail the speaker gave. Do not add requirements the speaker did not ask for.
triggers.author: Whisper Unchained
triggers.description: A loose spoken request becomes a well-structured prompt for another AI.

triggers.name: Feature spec
triggers.prompt:
Rewrite the text as a short feature specification in Markdown with these headings:

## Summary
Two or three sentences: what the feature is and who it is for.

## How it works
A numbered list of what the user does and what the product does in response.

## Acceptance criteria
A checklist ("- [ ] ...") of statements that can each be tested as true or false.

## Edge cases
Bullet points for unusual situations the speaker mentioned or that follow directly from what they said.

## Open questions
Bullet points for decisions the speaker left unclear. Leave this heading out if there are none.

Stay with what the speaker described. Do not design extra features.
triggers.author: Whisper Unchained
triggers.description: A spoken feature idea becomes a short spec with acceptance criteria.

triggers.name: Bullet list
triggers.prompt:
Rewrite the text as a bullet list.

- One point per line, each starting with "- ".
- Keep each point short: cut filler and repeated words, keep every fact.
- Keep the order the speaker used.
- No heading, no introduction line and no closing line.
triggers.author: Whisper Unchained
triggers.description: Your dictation as a tidy bullet list, one point per line.

triggers.name: Chat message
triggers.prompt:
Rewrite the text as a short message for a work chat app such as Slack or Teams.

- Friendly and direct, as you would write to a colleague. No greeting line and no sign-off.
- Lead with the point or the question.
- At most a few short lines. Use "•" bullets only when there are three or more separate items.
- No headings. No Markdown except *bold* around a deadline or a name that must not be missed.
- Keep every fact, name, time and number exactly as spoken.
triggers.author: Whisper Unchained
triggers.description: A short, friendly message for Slack, Teams or Discord.

triggers.name: Markdown
triggers.prompt:
Rewrite the text as well-structured Markdown.

- Add a "#" title only if the text clearly has one topic that can be named in a few words.
- Use "##" headings where the speaker moves to a new subject.
- Turn spoken lists into "-" bullet lists, and steps in order into numbered lists.
- Put commands, code, file names and paths in backticks.
- Use **bold** sparingly, for the few words that matter most.

Keep the speaker's wording and every detail. Only fix the layout, punctuation and obvious speech slips. Do not wrap the reply in a code block.
triggers.author: Whisper Unchained
triggers.description: Your dictation, laid out as proper Markdown with headings and lists.

triggers.name: Regular expression
triggers.prompt:
The text describes a pattern the speaker wants to match. Reply with one regular expression that matches it and nothing else.

- Use syntax that works in most engines (PCRE, Python, JavaScript) unless the speaker names one.
- Do not wrap it in slashes, quotes or a code block.
- Prefer the simplest pattern that is correct. Anchor it with ^ and $ only if the speaker wants the whole text to match.
triggers.author: Whisper Unchained
triggers.description: Describe the pattern in words; get the regular expression.

triggers.name: Shell command
triggers.prompt:
The text describes something the speaker wants to do on the command line. Reply with the command that does it and nothing else.

- Write it for PowerShell on Windows unless the speaker names another shell or system (bash, zsh, Linux, macOS, cmd).
- One line where possible. Join steps with the shell's own chaining operator.
- Use standard built-in commands. Do not assume extra tools are installed unless the speaker names them.
- Where a real value is needed that the speaker did not give, use an obvious placeholder in capitals such as PATH_TO_FOLDER.
- No explanation, no comments, no code block markers.
triggers.author: Whisper Unchained
triggers.description: Say what you want done; get the command to paste into a terminal.

triggers.name: Spreadsheet formula
triggers.prompt:
The text describes a calculation the speaker wants in a spreadsheet. Reply with one formula that does it and nothing else.

- Start with "=".
- Use functions that work in both Excel and Google Sheets unless the speaker names one of them.
- Use the cells, columns or ranges the speaker mentioned. Where none were given, use A1-style placeholders starting at A2.
- No explanation and no code block markers.
triggers.author: Whisper Unchained
triggers.description: Describe the calculation; get an Excel or Google Sheets formula.

triggers.name: Write it in Python
triggers.prompt:
The text describes what a piece of code should do. Reply with Python code that does it and nothing else.

- Python 3, standard library only unless the speaker names a package.
- Clear names, type hints on function signatures, and a one-line docstring on each function.
- Handle the obvious failure cases the description implies. Do not add features that were not asked for.
- No explanation before or after the code and no code block markers.
triggers.author: Whisper Unchained
triggers.description: Describe what the code should do; get the Python.

triggers.name: Client update
triggers.prompt:
Rewrite the text as a short progress update to a customer.

- Start with "Hi," or with the customer's name if the speaker gave one.
- Say what has been done, what happens next and when, and anything the customer needs to decide or pay for, in that order.
- Plain, polite and confident. No trade jargon without a few words of explanation.
- Keep every date, time and amount exactly as spoken. Do not add a price, a date or a promise that the speaker did not give.
- End with "Thanks," on its own line.
triggers.author: Whisper Unchained
triggers.description: Rough job notes become a polite progress message for a customer.

triggers.name: Clinical note (SOAP)
triggers.prompt:
Organise the text as a clinical note with exactly these four headings:

Subjective
Objective
Assessment
Plan

Put each thing the clinician said under the heading it belongs to, in short clinical sentences or "-" bullet points. Keep every value, dose, unit, duration and medication name exactly as spoken.

This is a strict reorganisation. Never add a finding, diagnosis, value, dose or plan that was not said. If nothing was said for a heading, write "Not documented" under it.
triggers.author: Whisper Unchained
triggers.description: A clinician's spoken summary, organised as Subjective, Objective, Assessment, Plan.

triggers.name: Property listing
triggers.prompt:
Rewrite the text as a property listing description.

- One paragraph of 80 to 120 words, starting with the strongest feature the speaker mentioned.
- Then a "-" bullet list of the key facts given: bedrooms, bathrooms, size, parking, outdoor space, location.
- Warm and specific. No clichés such as "must see" or "won't last", and no exclamation marks.
- Include only features and numbers the speaker stated. Never guess a size, price, year or distance.
triggers.author: Whisper Unchained
triggers.description: A spoken walk-through of a property becomes a listing description.

triggers.name: Fits in a post
triggers.prompt:
Rewrite the text as a single social media post of at most 280 characters, counting spaces.

- Keep the speaker's main point and their voice.
- No hashtags and no emoji unless the speaker used them.
- If it cannot all fit, keep the main point and drop the supporting detail. Never go over 280 characters.
triggers.author: Whisper Unchained
triggers.description: Your point in 280 characters or fewer, for X, Bluesky or Threads.

triggers.name: Half the length
triggers.prompt:
Rewrite the text in about half as many words.

- Keep every fact, name, number, date and request.
- Cut repetition, filler, hedging and throat-clearing first.
- Keep the speaker's tone and point of view.
- Keep the same format: if it was one paragraph, reply with one paragraph.
triggers.author: Whisper Unchained
triggers.description: The same message in about half the words.

triggers.name: Plain English
triggers.prompt:
Rewrite the text in plain English that a general reader can follow on the first read.

- Short sentences and everyday words. Explain any term a newcomer would not know in a few words, or replace it.
- Keep every fact, number, name and condition. Do not leave out caveats.
- Keep roughly the same length and the same order.
- Do not talk down to the reader and do not add opinions.
triggers.author: Whisper Unchained
triggers.description: Dense or technical text, rewritten so anyone can follow it.

triggers.name: Translate to Spanish
triggers.prompt:
Translate the text into natural, everyday Spanish, the way a native speaker would write it.

- Keep the meaning, the tone and the level of formality. Use "tú" unless the text is clearly formal.
- Keep names, brands, numbers and web addresses unchanged.
- Fix obvious speech slips as you translate. Do not add or leave out anything.

To make this trigger for another language, copy it and change "Spanish" in the name, the phrase and this instruction.
triggers.author: Whisper Unchained
triggers.description: Speak in your own language; paste natural Spanish.

triggers.name: Journal entry
triggers.prompt:
Rewrite the text as a personal journal entry in the first person.

- Keep the speaker's own words and feelings. Only remove filler, repetition and false starts, and add paragraph breaks where the subject changes.
- Do not add reflections, advice or a summary of your own.
- If the speaker mentioned things they need to do, add a line "To do:" at the end followed by a "-" bullet list of them. Leave that part out if there were none.
- No date and no title.
triggers.author: Whisper Unchained
triggers.description: A spoken brain dump becomes a tidy entry, with to-dos pulled out underneath.

triggers.name: Recipe
triggers.prompt:
Rewrite the text as a recipe with these parts:

The name of the dish on the first line.
Ingredients: a "-" bullet list, one ingredient per line with its amount first, in the order they are used.
Method: a numbered list, one action per step, with times and temperatures where the speaker gave them.
Notes: tips or substitutions the speaker mentioned. Leave this part out if there were none.

Keep every amount, time and temperature exactly as spoken. If an amount was not given, list the ingredient without one. Do not invent steps.
triggers.author: Whisper Unchained
triggers.description: A recipe told out loud becomes an ingredient list and numbered steps.

triggers.name: Mean mode
triggers.prompt:
Rewrite the text as the reply the speaker would actually post. The text is their unstructured, dictated brain dump: they are witty and condescending, and they are firing back at someone online (often a reply to a TikTok comment or a social media post). You are their ghostwriter.

Clean it up the way a copy editor would (drop the ums, filler and false starts, add punctuation, fix obvious speech-to-text errors), but you have some creative freedom: you may reword and sharpen it, as long as you don't change the overall message.

Do this:
1. Figure out the reasoning failure the OTHER person is making (are they confidently wrong, ignoring evidence, faking expertise, just slow, closed-minded?). The brain dump tells you what the other person got wrong; that flaw is your target.
2. Reorganize the speaker's scattered thoughts into a tight, clear, succinct reply. Keep every point they actually made; cut the rambling.
3. Mirror the SPEAKER'S own voice and speech pattern from the brain dump (their slang, rhythm, and casualness). You are writing AS the speaker, not to them. Do not sound like an AI.
4. Use exactly one line from the insult list below, from the group that matches the other person's specific reasoning failure, or something very much like one of them, reworded so it flows naturally in the speaker's voice. Pick the one that fits THIS argument; don't fall back on the same line every time. Where a line has a note in brackets, follow it.

Hard formatting rules:
- Plain text only. No markdown, no bullet points, no headings.
- NEVER use em dashes or en dashes. Use commas, periods, or ellipses.
- No hashtags and no emoji unless the speaker used them first.
- Keep it short enough for a social media reply.
- Output ONLY the finished reply. No preamble, no quotes around it, no explanation of what you did.

Example of the idea (not a script to copy): the brain dump 'I can't believe just uh how dumb you really are to think the earth is flat' could become 'Wow, just wow. I can't believe how dumb you have to be to think the Earth is flat...' followed by a fitting line from the insult list. NOT 'Holy gee willikers, this guy is a dumb dumb stupid head': that one has no line from the list and drops the flat-Earth point.

Example brain dump: 'the bible isn't real, if it was we'd expect talking snakes and burning bushes to talk too'
Example reply: 'The bible isn't real. If it was, we'd expect the talking snakes and burning bushes to still be talking, right? Look, I could explain it further, but I left my crayons at home.'

Insults, grouped by the reasoning failure they target:

Confidently wrong / overconfident
- I have never been so impressed with anyone's ability to be this wrong.
- You have the confidence of someone who's never Googled themselves.
- I am honored to witness your impressive lack of understanding.
- Your ignorance is an absolute triumph of human existence.

Ignores evidence / allergic to facts
- I admire how you never let evidence interfere with your opinions.
- Don't let my knowledge get in the way of your confidence.
- You have a rare talent for speaking at length without disturbing the facts.
- You're not wrong, you're just operating in a different intellectual timezone.

Fakes expertise / unearned authority
- You've mastered the tone of authority without the inconvenience of depth.
- It's interesting what you've done with your education.
- As an outsider, what are your views on intelligence?
- You're the reason instructions have drawings.
- I don't think either one of us knows what you're talking about.

Just not very bright / slow on the uptake
- I refuse to engage in a battle of wits with an unarmed man.
- I can explain it to you, but I can't understand it for you.
- I could explain it to you, but I left my crayons at home.
- Light travels faster than sound. That's why some people appear bright until you hear them speak.
- When it comes to thinking, you travel light.
- It's impossible to underestimate you.
- You're clearly intelligent, it just doesn't show up where it matters.
- Intelligence pursues you, but you appear to be a master of evasion.
- It's truly remarkable that you are the strongest swimmer your father had.
- You absolute WiFi-dependent potato. (swap "WiFi-dependent" for something from their text)
- You ain't the dumbest guy in the world, but you'd better hope he doesn't die.
- I bet you're the kind of person who'd climb over a glass wall to see what's on the other side.

Closed-minded / refuses to learn
- I can see you are committed to your current level of understanding.
- I can see why that makes sense to you.
- I love how you think outside the box; it's clear no one's ever invited you in.
- I wish I didn't have common sense. You seem so happy.

Lazy / dead weight
- I know you're not afraid of hard work. I've seen you stand near it all day.
- How long are you planning to be new at this?
- You're like a rusty rifle: you won't work, and you can't be fired.
- You do what you can, and I'll do what you can't.

Adds nothing / wasted everyone's time
- Thank you for helping me. It was like doing it myself, only harder.
- You have a unique way of contributing without adding much.
- Your food for thought leaves everyone hungry.
- I admire your courage to speak in the absence of knowledge.

Just unpleasant to be around
- I'm jealous of everyone that hasn't met you.
- Nothing lights up a room like your absence.
- You absolutely light up every room you walk out of.
- You have a special way of speaking that makes people appreciate your silence.
- You think your parents ever get tired of waiting to be proud of you?
triggers.author: Whisper Unchained
triggers.description: Turns your rough thoughts into a short, cutting comeback in your own voice.
